land.text: Klarjeti, the Bagratids' 'patrimonial Duchy' on the upper Chorokhi

predecessors.note: The infobox lists 'Principality of Iberia; Arminiya' as predecessors; the Iberian princely line moves its seat from Kartli to Klarjeti in 813.

land.text: Bagrat III, 'King of the Georgians', unites Iberia with Abkhazia on his father Gurgen's death in 1008

successors.note: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Georgia row starts in 1010 and its Georgia row runs 980-1009.

land.text: David III's Tao, claimed by Basil II after David's death in 1000/1001

successors.note: Scope disputed (the 979 'Upper Lands' only, or all of Tao/Tayk up to Lake Van).

capitals.name: Artanuji (Ardanuc)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Artanuji Bana'; the Principality page dates Artanuji to c. 813-888. After 888 the page gives no other seat.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the founding year, which Cliopatria lacks (its first shape is 814). 'In 813, the last Iberian prince Ashot I of the Bagrationi dynasty established himself in his patrimonial Duchy of Klarjeti'; Klarjeti is read as the modern Artvin province (a reading, not the page's boundary). The ledger's 814 shape carries the whole Tao-Klarjeti realm.

Cliopatria's 24,351 km2 (bbox 40.4-43.6E, 40.2-41.6N) lies on Tao-Klarjeti and Javakheti in Turkey and Georgia. The page names Tbilisi, Kakheti, Kartli, Tao, Klarjeti, Javakheti and Artanuji but gives no area and no boundary, and its 814-887 coverage is sparse (c. 818, 853, 876, 880-882 only), so the shape is accepted at the honest precision of the era.
Area 24,327 km2 against 24,351 (-0.1 percent): redrawing noise; the page records no change of land in 825.
Area 24,351 km2 (+0.1 percent): noise; no change of land on the page in 840. In 853 Bagrat I regained central Iberia (Kartli) only briefly, which Cliopatria does not draw here.
Area 24,207 km2 (-0.6 percent): noise; the page has nothing for 866. Before 876 'Guaram handed over some of his possessions to his brothers' (a family division, not a loss of state).

Area 24,614 km2 (+1.7 percent): noise, no event on the page. The shape runs 886-989 unchanged although the page records fragmentation among Bagratid branches ('David II's (r. 923-937) control was limited to Javakheti and Artaani'; in 958 Bagrat II 'only ruled Lower Tao') and a gain of Phasiane from Byzantium in c. 952 (outside the shape, which stops at 40.16N): treat the frontier as soft. Kartli, which Gurgen and Bagrat III held from 976, is drawn by Cliopatria's Georgia row, not here.

Same extent as 886 (24,614 km2). Valid to 999 as Cliopatria draws it; the page keeps the kingdom to 1008 (Bagrat III 'crowned as King of Iberia on the death of Bagrat II in 994'; Gurgen 994-1008). See the new keyframes for 1000-1008.

correction.text: unchanged 990-999 shape carried through 1000, the year David III of Tao died

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1000: Cliopatria's row ends in 999 but the kingdom lives to 1008. 'On 31 March 1000' David III died (the David III page gives 1000 or 1001), so the shape is carried unchanged for the year.

correction.text: Tao-Klarjeti without Tao, annexed by Basil II after David III's death

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1001-1008: the 999 shape without Tao, which Byzantium claimed on David III's death (Basil II 'marched north-eastward to claim the lands David had promised to the emperor' and Bagrat, 'unable to prevent the annexation of David's realm, had to recognize the new borders in reward of the imperial title of kouropalates' [quote corrected to the page wording, reviewer eu-19-c]). Pages disagree on scope: the Bagrat III page says the emperor 'completed the conquest of Tao-Klarjeti' within months, yet lists Klarjeti among Bagrat's lands; the David III page says scholars disagree whether only the 979 'Upper Lands' or all Tao/Tayk passed. Klarjeti is kept (conf 1). 'Tao' is not yet in the gazetteer.

ledger.note: 813: Ashot I settles in Klarjeti and founds the Bagratid line that rules Iberia from Artanuji. 'In 813, the last Iberian prince Ashot I of the Bagrationi dynasty established himself in his patrimonial Duchy of Klarjeti'; infobox 'Principality (c. 813-888)'. The year and the duchy are the page's, the reading of Klarjeti as the Artvin province is not.

853: Bagrat I regains central Iberia. 'In 853, now supporting Bugha al-Kabir, Bagrat regained central Iberia, but only for a brief time.' The page does not say who held central Iberia in 853; the counterpart is the Arab emir of Tbilisi, the Bagratids' 'traditional foe' (880).
854: the Bagratid hold on central Iberia is over. The page says only 'for a brief time'; the year is bridging.

888: Adarnase restores the Iberian kingship, and the principality becomes a kingdom. The kingdom 'emerged circa 888 AD, succeeding the Principality of Iberia'; the infobox changes the government from 'Principality (c. 813-888)' to 'Feudal Monarchy (888-1008)'. Smbat I of Armenia 'personally crowned' Adarnase in 899 and Byzantium recognised him as curopalates in 891. Same state, same colour.

c. 952: Phasiane comes from the Byzantine emperor. 'He also received Phasiane from the Byzantine emperor in c. 952.' The page's preceding bullet names the ruler as Ashot II (r. 937-954) [reviewer eu-19-c]; Phasiane (the Pasinler plain east of Erzurum) lies south of Cliopatria's shape, which stops at 40.16N.

1001: Byzantium annexes David III's Tao. 'David was murdered by his nobles early in 1000 or 1001' (Aristakes: 28 March 1001; the Bagrat III page: 31 March 1000); Basil II 'marched north-eastward to claim the lands David had promised to the emperor' and Bagrat, 'unable to prevent the annexation of David's realm, had to recognize the new borders in reward of the imperial title of kouropalates' [quote corrected to the page wording, reviewer eu-19-c]. The year is disputed (1000 or 1001); the extent is disputed (see the 1001 keyframe).

region.text: Tao-Klarjeti without Tao, Klarjeti held by the Iberian crown

ledger.note: 1008: Bagrat III unites Iberia and Abkhazia. 'In 1008, following the death of his father Gurgen I, Bagrat inherited the hereditary title of King of the Georgians'; the infobox gives the kingdom's end as 1008 and the Kingdom of Georgia as successor. Cliopatria's Iberians row ends in 999 and its Georgia row (980-1009) already draws Abkhazia with Kartli.

wars.name: Abkhazian invasion of Iberia (903-904)
wars.outcome: Constantine III of Abkhazia dispossessed Adarnase in 904 and was then defeated by Adarnase together with an ally the page calls 'the two men'; no change of land is recorded for the Iberians.
wars.note: The two sentences ('Adarnase was dispossessed by Constantine III in 904'; 'The two men collaborated in defeating, in 904, the Abkhazian king Constantine III') are not tied to places on the page. The Smbat I page (opened for bagratid-armenia) has the Abkhazians raiding Gugark and Iberia in 903 and Smbat annexing Abkhazian districts including Klarjeti and Ardahan.

wars.name: Revolt of Bardas Phokas (987-989)
wars.outcome: David III of Tao joined the revolt and was defeated in 989; in c. 990 he was granted the title of kuropalates again on condition that his lands would revert to Byzantium at his death.
wars.note: The Kingdom page: 'The only setback was the 987-989 unsuccessful conflict with the Byzantine Empire.' The article title for the revolt was not checked.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary or area for any year; the shape is Tao-Klarjeti in modern Turkey and Georgia and the Bagratid branches divided it among themselves.

notes:
ROW TO STATE. Cliopatria's Kingdom of the Iberians (814-999) draws only Tao-Klarjeti (centroid Artvin, 24-25 k km2). The Wikipedia state of the same name (888-1008) also includes Kartli under Gurgen (994-1008) and Bagrat III, which Cliopatria draws in its Georgia row (980-1009, 61 k km2). The georgia/kingdom-of-abkhazia dossiers of eu-19 should know that Kartli 976-1008 is Iberian by the page but is drawn as Georgia.

START. 813 (Ashot I in Klarjeti) is taken as the start although Cliopatria begins in 814 and the page's infobox says 'Established: 888': the infobox's own government field reads 'Principality (c. 813-888)'. The principality-of-iberia dossier ends in 813 and hands over to this one; the 888 change is a rename (principality to kingdom), not a new state.

END. 1008 (page) against 999 (Cliopatria). 1000-1008 are new keyframes. The loss of Tao is dated 1001 (the David III page: 'early in 1000 or 1001'; Georgian Chronicles, Aristakes, Asoghik and Samuel Anetsi give 1001) although the Bagrat III page has 31 March 1000. Whether Klarjeti stayed with the crown is disputed between the two pages.

NOT RECORDED. The 899 crowning by Smbat I of Armenia, the 891 Byzantine curopalate title and the 818 caliphal recognition are status changes, not land: the suzerain or patron dossiers (byzantine-empire, abbasid-caliphate) should carry any vassal_start. Fragmentation among Bagratid branches (923-937 David II limited to Javakheti and Artaani; 958 Bagrat II only Lower Tao) has no dated frontier on the page.

GAZETTEER. 'Tao' (region) and the Phasiane coordinate need gazetteer entries; Klarjeti is read as Artvin province.

MISSING DOSSIERS. kingdom-of-abkhazia (778-1008; Cliopatria's Georgia row) and emirate-of-tbilisi (736-1122) are counterparts here and need dossiers. Rulers are not given: the page's king table was not read in full.
